title: Find, understand, and organize your files with private local AI
subtitle: A personal file copilot that searches what your files mean and turns every change into a plan you control.
description: Sift is a private local file copilot for natural-language search, multimodal retrieval, and safe AI-assisted organization on macOS.

hero.alt: Sift creates a folder organization plan and presents it for review
hero.caption: Sift proposes a coherent folder structure, clearer filenames, and a complete before-and-after plan.

abstract: Sift helps you find a file when you remember its meaning but not its name. It searches filenames, document contents, and indexed images, then shows the evidence behind every result.

When a folder needs attention, Sift can propose a structure or follow a plain-language instruction. Nothing moves until you review the plan. You can edit destinations, skip files, apply selected changes, and undo the most recent batch. All models and file data stay on your computer.

highlights.label: Files and models stay on your Mac
Every change starts as an editable plan

sections.title: Find what you remember
sections.lead: Ask in your own words and verify the evidence behind every result.

blocks.text: Search for a topic, an invoice, a paper, or a half-remembered phrase. Sift retrieves relevant files even when your wording does not match the filename, then shows the matching document text so you can confirm the result.

blocks.alt: Sift finds a relevant document from a natural-language question
blocks.caption: Natural-language retrieval over filenames and document contents.

sections.title: Search what is inside an image
sections.lead: Make screenshots searchable by visible text and visual context, not only by filename.

blocks.text: Enable image reading during a scan and a local vision model can index screenshots and photos. This makes it possible to find a slide, receipt, chart, or captured conversation from what appears inside it.

blocks.alt: Sift finds a screenshot by the text and visual content inside it
blocks.caption: Multimodal retrieval powered by a local vision model.

sections.title: Turn intent into a safe plan
sections.lead: Organize a whole folder or simply tell Sift what outcome you want.

blocks.text: Sift reviews the complete batch and proposes categories, subfolders, and clearer filenames together. You can also ask it to move, rename, group, or trash a set of files in plain English. Both paths produce the same reviewable plan.

blocks.alt: Sift converts a plain-language move request into an editable plan
blocks.caption: A plain-language instruction becomes a before-and-after plan.

items.title: Review first
items.text: Nothing changes until you approve the plan.

items.title: Edit anything
items.text: Change destinations, skip files, or apply only selected rows.

items.title: Undo safely
items.text: Reverse the latest batch, including files moved to the Trash.

sections.title: More than a file sorter
sections.lead: Sift combines understanding, retrieval, and organization in one private local workflow.

items.title: Your models
items.text: Choose compatible chat, embedding, and vision models installed in Ollama.

items.title: Your data
items.text: Filenames, document text, images, prompts, and embeddings remain local.

items.title: Your decision
items.text: Model output stays a suggestion until you choose to apply it.

sections.title: Start with one double-click
sections.lead: The initial release supports macOS and creates a familiar app icon for everyday use.

items: Download Sift from GitHub and unzip the folder.
Double-click Install Sift.command once to download the default local models and prepare the app.
Open Sift from the blue Sift.app icon revealed in Finder.

blocks.text: Sift currently integrates with Finder, the macOS Trash, and a native macOS launcher. Windows and Linux are not officially supported in this initial release.
